st.headline: US flags Singapore as part of China’s ‘shadow transshipment network’ that avoids Trump’s tariffs
st.teaser: The US says 40 lower-tariff countries have become the launchpads and hubs of a new evasion architecture.
fullText: SINGAPORE – Singapore and dozens of other countries are at risk of being used by Chinese exporters to avoid US tariffs, President Donald Trump’s administration said on Aug 13.
A report issued by the White House, titled “The Great Transshipment Scam,” frames the routing of Chinese goods through an intermediate lower-tariffed country by concealing the true origin.
It also said the administration will use an artificial intelligence-powered “Detective Border”, among other initiatives, to help crack down on illegal transshipments.
“The message to the world is simple. The age of untraceable illegal transshipment is over,” the report said.

The report does not say what immediate action will follow. In August 2025, the US announced an additional 40 per cent tariff specifically on goods determined to have been illegally transshipped to evade duties.

Using estimates from government and private-sector studies, the report estimates that tariff-evading transshipments may have robbed the US of customs revenue in the range of US$40 billion (S$51.2 billion) to US$303 billion.

“The available data show a substantial reallocation of US import sourcing following the 2018 tariffs. As China’s direct share of US goods imports declined, the combined share supplied by identified transshipment countries increased,” the White House report said.

It added that the 40 lower-tariff countries have become the launchpads and hubs of a new evasion architecture, namely “products made largely in China, lightly touched abroad and exported to America under new identities”.
But this relationship does not establish that all displaced Chinese trade was illegally transshipped.

“Some of the shift reflects legitimate changes in production, investment and sourcing. However, the timing, magnitude and direction of the two trends support further investigation of the extent to which tariffed goods were rerouted through third countries.”
The 40 countries, including Singapore, identified in the report as participants in the “shadow transshipment network”, were grouped into three tiers.
The White House placed Singapore in Tier 3, which the report said consists of “small, opportunistic Chinese targets”.

“These are smaller economies with lower absolute illegal transshipment volumes but specific weak-link advantages – including low-cost labour, free zones, port or border access, bonded warehousing, niche assembly capacity, preferential US access or limited customs enforcement capacity – that make them attractive opportunistic targets for China-linked rerouting.”
The report also said China-linked exporters may use these jurisdictions for both limited production activity and logistics side-routing.

The report warned the 40 countries that as their local export sectors and transportation networks become increasingly dependent on Chinese inputs, logistics and capital, “Beijing may gain additional commercial and geopolitical leverage while preserving indirect access to the US market”.
The Straits Times has asked the Ministry of Trade and Industry for comments on the White House report.
But Singapore has repeatedly stated in the past that it takes trade compliance seriously.

Singapore Customs, in response to media queries in September 2025, said: “Singapore’s legislative and regulatory framework governing transshipment is consistent with international best practices and rules, including those from the World Customs Organization, and seeks to facilitate trade through greater transparency and predictability for businesses.” The agency added that transshipment in Singapore refers to the movement of goods from their source to their destination via Singapore, involving a change from one conveyance to another.

“Transshipped goods do not originate from Singapore and are not for domestic circulation or storage. Their transshipment through Singapore does not change their country of origin (i.e. they cannot be relabelled as originating from Singapore).”

Companies transshipping goods through Singapore must fully comply with the Republic’s laws and regulations, said Singapore Customs, adding that the agency works closely with international counterparts to detect and take action against illicit goods imported, exported or transshipped through the nation .
The report is part of the Trump administration’s efforts to rebuild the US leader’s tariff regime after it was undermined by a court decision earlier in 2026.

In July, a new 12.5 per cent levy, covering about a third of Singapore’s domestic exports to the US, was imposed after White House alleged that t he Republic and dozens of other economies failed to adopt and effectively enforce prohibitions on trade in goods produced with forced labour.

cna.headline: Marina Bay Sands to host Ferrari race car, luxury pop-up and F1-themed events ahead of Singapore Grand Prix
cna.teaser: Ferrari will take over Marina Bay Sands this F1 season with various events and activities, including a Ferrari SF21 show car going on display from Sep 14 to Oct 12.
fullText: Formula 1 fans in Singapore can get a closer look at a Ferrari race car and see Marina Bay Sands (MBS) lit up in Ferrari red as part of a series of activities taking place around this year's Singapore night race season.
The activities begin in September, with a show car of the Ferrari SF21 going on display at the MBS Tower 1 hotel lobby from Sep 14 to Oct 12.
The car will be displayed ahead of the Singapore Grand Prix, taking place from Oct 9 to 11 at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

There will also be a Ferrari Lifestyle boutique at The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands from Sep 25 to Oct 25, offering an immersive expression of the Ferrari universe beyond the world of Formula 1. The pop-up also marks the first time the Ferrari Lifestyle boutique has been brought to Asia.

From Sep 28 to Oct 11, MBS will also hold Home of Champions, a destination-wide programme featuring a series of F1-themed events, such as motorsport talks, luxury retail pop-ups and exclusive dining experiences.
As part of the programme, the resort's three hotel towers and ArtScience Museum will be illuminated in Ferrari red from 7pm to 11.59pm each evening, with the display visible across Marina Bay.
The activities are part of an extended collaboration between MBS and Scuderia Ferrari HP, which first began in 2023.

As part of the renewed partnership, MBS is also offering a S$100,000 (US$78,130) five-night hospitality package for up to two people during the Formula 1 season. It includes a stay in a Paiza Grand Suite, access to selected events and parties, three-day Paddock tickets and priority access to after-parties at Marquee Singapore. The package also includes dining experiences at Marina Bay Sands and meet-and-greet opportunities with Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
More information is also available at the official Singapore Night Race website .

listening.title: Singapore Banks Strengthen Security Measures Amid Scam Concerns
listening.transcript: As digital banking scams become increasingly sophisticated in Singapore, major local banks are rolling out tighter security measures. These measures include a 'kill switch' for customers to freeze their accounts instantly if they suspect fraud. While some consumers find the extra security steps cumbersome, authorities emphasise that safeguarding public funds remains the top priority.

economistArticle.title: The Great Unwinding: Japan’s Yen Rescue and the Threat to Global Markets
paras: For decades, global investors have relied on a remarkably simple and profitable strategy: borrowing cheap Japanese yen at near-zero interest rates to buy higher-yielding assets elsewhere. This phenomenon, known as the "carry trade," has funneled trillions of dollars into overseas equities, emerging markets, and high-yield corporate bonds. However, this massive house of cards is beginning to shudder as Tokyo takes direct action to prop up its currency.

The Bank of Japan’s recent shift away from negative interest rates, combined with active government intervention to buy yen, signals a historic turning point. By raising borrowing costs at home and strengthening the yen, policymakers are making the carry trade increasingly expensive to maintain. As investors rush to cover their short positions, they are forced to sell their global assets to buy back yen, triggering a reverse flow of capital.

This sudden repatriation of capital has sent ripples through international financial hubs. In Singapore and Hong Kong, wealth managers are closely monitoring how this liquidity withdrawal affects regional property markets and technology equities. The unwinding of such a colossal trade is rarely a gentle process; it often exacerbates volatility in markets accustomed to boundless cheap credit.

Proponents of the intervention argue that a dangerously weak yen was fueling domestic inflation and eroding the purchasing power of Japanese households. Yet, by defending its currency, Japan is inadvertently exporting financial instability. The delicate balance that global central banks must now strike is preventing this necessary adjustment from turning into a disorderly rout.

Ultimately, the death of the carry trade marks the end of an era of cheap money. As Tokyo unwinds its massive, decades-long monetary experiment, the global economy must brace for a new reality where capital actually has a cost. For investors who grew rich on the back of the yen’s weakness, the bill has finally arrived.
economistArticle.cn:
数十年来，全球投资者一直依赖一种非常简单且有利可图的策略：以接近于零的利率借入廉价的日元，去购买其他地方收益率更高的资产。这种被称为“套利交易”的现象已将数万亿美元注入海外股市、新兴市场和高收益公司债券。然而，随着东京采取直接行动支撑其货币，这个巨大的纸牌屋正开始震颤。

日本央行近期摆脱负利率的转变，加之政府主动干预购买日元，标志着一个历史性的转折点。通过提高国内借贷成本和强化日元，决策者们正在使套利交易的维持成本变得越来越高。随着投资者争相回购日元以补仓，他们被迫抛售全球资产来买回日元，从而引发了资金的反向流动。

这种突如其来的资本回流波及了各大国际金融中心。在新加坡和香港，财富管理经理们正密切关注这种流动性撤退对区域房地产市场和科技股的影响。如此庞大的交易平仓很少能温和进行；它往往会加剧习惯了无限廉价信贷的市场之波动。

干预的支持者认为，危险的弱势日元正在推高国内通胀，并侵蚀日本家庭的购买力。然而，通过保卫其货币，日本在无意中出口了金融不稳定。全球央行目前必须达到的微妙平衡是，防止这种必要的调整演变成一场无序的溃败。

归根结底，套利交易的终结标志着廉价货币时代的结束。随着东京结束其长达数十年、庞大的货币实验，全球经济必须为一个资本真正具有成本的新现实做好准备。对于那些依靠日元贬值而暴富的投资者来说，买单的时刻终于到了。

gems.s: This phenomenon, known as the "carry trade," has funneled trillions of dollars into overseas equities, emerging markets, and high-yield corporate bonds.
gems.why:
This sentence uses an appositive clause (known as the 'carry trade') to define a term cleanly within a sentence, and features parallel structure ('into X, Y, and Z') to group diverse elements smoothly. 

这句话使用同位语从句（known as the 'carry trade'）在句中清晰地定义了一个术语，并采用了平行结构（'into X, Y, and Z'）将多种不同的元素流畅地组合在一起。

gems.s: The delicate balance that global central banks must now strike is preventing this necessary adjustment from turning into a disorderly rout.
gems.why:
This sentence showcases a relative clause ('that global central banks must now strike') modifying the subject, and utilizes the gerund structure 'preventing... from' to outline a policy goal. 

这句话展示了一个关系从句（'that global central banks must now strike'）来修饰主语，并利用动名词结构 'preventing... from'（防止……变成……）来概述一个政策目标。
